meta.title: Canopi - Agroecological Design Tool
meta.description: Plan food forests, gardens and agroecological systems with Canopi. Free and open source for Linux, macOS and Windows, with a Web edition available in your browser.
footer.license: Free software under the AGPL-3.0 licence.
footer.association: Canopi is a non-profit association under French law (loi 1901).

climate.tropical.about: Warm in every month and no frost; the year turns on wet and dry seasons.
climate.subtropical.about: Hot, humid summers and mild winters with little frost, or mild highlands with a dry winter.
climate.mediterranean.about: Dry, warm to hot summers and mild, rainy winters.
climate.arid.about: Little rain, far less than the sun and wind dry out: deserts and steppes, hot or cold.
climate.temperate.about: Mild all year, with rain in every season, cool summers and light frosts.
climate.continental.about: Cold winters with lasting frost or snow, and warm to hot summers.
climate.boreal.about: Long, very cold winters and short, cool summers.
climate.title: What is your climate?

home.consortium.lede: A plant palette is a group of plants that help each other. Choose your climate: start from a suggestion of 6 to 12 plants, or build your own, up to hundreds.
home.consortium.note: A beta with curated plant lists for four climates so far: tropical, arid, Mediterranean and temperate; the other climates borrow the nearest list, checked against your location.

what.title: From a blank map to a planting plan
what.lede: Everything happens on the real map of your land.
what.map.title: Draw on your land
what.map.text: Find your site, outline it with zones, then place plants one by one or in rows. Measure and annotate over the map, satellite imagery or contours.
what.map.alt: Canopi with an example food forest on the map of Central Park, New York: planting belts in rings around a pond, with the tools around the map.
what.catalog.title: Find the right plants
what.catalog.text: Search {count} species by common or scientific name, filter them, and keep your favourites, in 11 languages.
what.catalog.alt: The plant catalog panel: a search box, filters and a list of species.
what.plan.title: Plan the work and the cost
what.plan.text: Schedule actions on a calendar, price each species in a budget, and see strata and succession in the consortium view.
what.plan.alt: The calendar panel: a month view and the planting actions scheduled for November.
what.export: When it’s ready, take it to the field: a planting-plan PDF with field sheets, GeoJSON, or your own .canopi file.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: What projectcanopi.com receives, what stays on your device, and which other services are contacted, and when.
privacy.site.title: Visiting the site
privacy.site.host: Canopi is a non-profit association under French law. Cloudflare hosts the site: like any web host, it receives each request your browser makes to projectcanopi.com, with your IP address. Requests that run the site’s own code, such as sending a form, are recorded in Cloudflare’s logs with the request’s details: the address requested, the time, your browser and an approximate location (such as city, country and network). The site’s code never logs what you wrote.
privacy.site.none: There is no account, no analytics and no advertising, and the site’s own code sets no cookies.
privacy.site.storage: Your browser keeps a few settings on this device: the light or dark theme, the climate you chose, the ticks in a guide’s checklists and, for this visit only, the fact that it already offered your language.
privacy.site.logs: Cloudflare keeps these logs for up to 7 days: {link}
privacy.tool.title: The plant palette tool
privacy.tool.device: The tool runs in your browser. It downloads the plant list, the climate files and the soil files from projectcanopi.com, and keeps your palette (with your height limit, plot size and spot answers), your country, your location and your site's climate on this device, in the browser's local storage. Your last spot answers are also kept to start your next palette. None of it is sent to Canopi. 'Forget this location' clears your location and your spot answers.
privacy.tool.share: A share link holds your palette after the # of the address, a part browsers never send to a server: only the people you give the link to can see it.
privacy.location.title: Your site’s location
privacy.location.device: If you let the tool use your device’s location, your browser asks your permission first. The location is used on your device to read the climate and the country, and saved only on this device.
privacy.location.tiles: To read the climate, your browser downloads whole files from projectcanopi.com, each covering about 1,000 km, so these downloads do not reveal the precise point. If you open the map, OpenFreeMap receives the area it shows; a place search sends the text you typed to Nominatim (see below).
privacy.location.link: A share link includes your place only if you tick 'Include my place', and then only as the centre of its climate-grid square (about 11 km north to south, narrower toward the poles), its country, your spot answers and your soil test.
privacy.location.search: Place search: when you press Enter, the text you typed goes to Nominatim, run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation, with what any website receives (your IP address, browser and language). Type a town or village, not your address.
privacy.location.map: Map: OpenFreeMap sends the map’s tiles and styles only once you open the map. It receives your IP address and the area the map shows.
privacy.contact.title: The contact form
privacy.contact.body: The contact form sends your name, your email address, your message and the page’s language to Canopi by email: Cloudflare delivers it to Canopi’s mailbox at Gmail (Google). They are used only to reply to you, and the site keeps no copy.
privacy.correction.title: Suggesting a correction
privacy.correction.body: In the plant palette tool, the correction form sends the plant, the value it shows, your suggestion and your note, the data release, the list the plant is placed from, the climate you chose and the page’s language to Canopi by email, the same way. Before sending, you agree that your suggestion may be published in Canopi’s plant data under CC BY-SA 4.0.
privacy.correction.email: Your email address is optional: if you give it, it is used only to reply to you and is never published.
privacy.donate.title: Donations
privacy.donate.body: The donation form belongs to HelloAsso, a French payment platform for associations. It loads only when you open the donation window, and what you enter there goes to HelloAsso, under its own privacy policy.
privacy.ask.title: Questions
privacy.ask.body: To ask what Canopi holds about you, or to have a message deleted, write to us through the {link}.
dataSources.tool.title: The plant palette tool: climate, places and maps
dataSources.tool.lede: The plant palette tool reads your site’s climate and country from the canopi-climate grid, and the plants’ observed climate ranges from GBIF occurrences (thinned to one per climate cell), with TreeGOER’s tree ranges where they are stricter. Names, citations and licences appear as their sources publish them.

consortium.palette.chart.saved: Your palette is saved on this device.
consortium.palette.yearsIntroPhone: Who stands where as the plot grows up. Step through time; an empty light level is a hole.
consortium.palette.yearsIntroMany: Who stands where as the plot grows up. Each light level shows how many plants stand in it and the first three names. A level opens in place to its first 10 names, then “+ more”.
consortium.palette.readYears: Each row is a light level: Full sun at the top, then Mostly sun, Part shade, and Shade at the bottom. A plant stands in the level it is planted in; its details say every level it grows in. Step through time to see who stands where: the years say when a plant has its place in the palette, not how long it lives. A dashed place is a hole: nobody stands there then.
consortium.palette.readFigures: “Your place in figures” lists everything the checks use and where each value comes from: the climate map, the soil map, your value, your answer, “Not known: no data for your place” or “Not answered”. “Your value” is one you set; a temperature, rain or dry-months value of yours is kept as a shift, the same in every period, and Reset goes back to the map, or to not answered. A plant’s Sources say where each value comes from. “Light: estimate, from PFAF” was filled in from that work. “Light: AI estimate, no source” comes from an AI model’s general knowledge only: no work stands behind it.

consortium.palette.goalExplain: At least this many plants for each job, in every time span from year 1 to year 60. Two means one can fail. Fewer is “thin”, a next step after the holes. There is no upper limit: past {n} a job only says how many. Light levels have no such number: an empty one is a hole.

consortium.palette.jobsFoot: A plant counts under every job it does.

consortium.palette.readJobs: In Jobs, the strip is the seven time spans. A gap shorter than a year, and the time after year 60, are not judged: a thin line, never a hole.
consortium.palette.readUnknown: A row with no toxicity mark has not been checked, or nothing was recorded. An unknown is never shown as a hole, a “no” or a filled level: where a plant’s jobs or light are not checked yet, the line says so, as in “Covers the ground: nobody known after year 25 · 2 plants not checked” or “Shade: 1 plant fits, 2 unknown”.
consortium.palette.readSyntropic: If you know syntropic farming: the four light levels are the strata, and the time spans are the stages of succession.
consortium.block.end: End of the consortium stream blocks: every stream adds its keys above this line, after its own block key.
